provenance.subject: single-floor derivation: the AC derive script refuses an incomplete policy before lock work, and refuses a partial floor application at lock verification
provenance.design_reference: docs/aben-design.md section 9, B3, and section 5 for the ordered derivation contract

repository_state.note: AC backend/pyproject.toml at this commit declares version 0.7.15 (re-observed 2026-08-14). The preserved launcher-string variant that this row reconstructs is recorded verbatim in the aweb-aben task record, not duplicated here - a second transcription of a string whose exactness is the point would be a second thing to drift.

control_one.mutation: delete a policy row from derive_release_floors.py's total artifact-to-floor map
control_one.refusal: incomplete-derivation, raised at step (a), the domain check
control_one.why: step (a) requires incoming key set == policy key set exactly, either direction. This is the independent completeness fact: a policy row deletion fails HERE and not later, and a new train artifact with no AC decision fails closed.

control_two.mutation: force a partial floor application (one floor moved, the other left stale)
control_two.refusal: lock verification at step (e), naming package/wanted/got
control_two.why: this is the near-miss made permanent: the single-floor derive would have silently shipped the old server in ac-image. The refusal must name both the wanted and the got version, or it cannot distinguish this from any other lock failure.
